It has also been said that what is meant by the verse is voluntary prayer (tatawwuʿ). It could be said that there is no reference to prayer in the verse, but rather what is meant is glorification (tasbih) during these times, that is, the saying of one who says "Glory be to God." That would not be far from correct. Glorification during these times, although it may be applied to prayer, is metaphorical (majaz), and the literal meaning (haqiqah) takes priority unless there is an indicator that turns it toward the figurative sense. His saying: ﴿so that you may be pleased﴾ is connected to "so glorify": that is, glorify during these times in hope that you will attain from God, glorified is He, what your soul is pleased with. This is according to the reading of the majority. Al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim read (turda, "you are pleased") with a damma on the taʾ in the passive voice, meaning: your Lord will be pleased with you.

﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to of them, as pairs﴾. The exegesis of this verse has already been given in al-Hijr. The meaning is: do not prolong the gaze of your eyes. "Azwajan" is the object (maf'ul) of "We have given enjoyment." "Zahrata" is in the accusative, either as a circumstantial accusative (hal) or governed by an implied verb, meaning "We made" or "We gave." Al-Zajjaj mentioned this meaning. It has also been said that it is a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in "with it," with regard to its position, which is the accusative, not with regard to its form, since it is in the genitive, as you say "I passed by him, your brother." Al-Farra' preferred the accusative as a circumstantial accusative, and it is permissible that it be a substitute, and it is permissible that it be in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar), like ﴿the dye of God﴾ and ﴿the promise of God﴾ and ﴿the splendor of the worldly life﴾. Its meaning is its adornment and brilliance with plants and other things. ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar read (zahrata) with a fatha on the ha', which is the blossom of plants. The lam in "that We may test them therein" is connected to "We have given enjoyment": that is, that We make that a trial for them and a misguidance, as a test from Us for them, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them﴾ [al-Kahf: 7]. It has also been said: that We may punish them. And it has been said: that We may make the obligations heavier upon them. ﴿And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting﴾, that is, the reward of God, and what He has stored up for His righteous servants in the Hereafter is better than what He provided them in this world in every state. Moreover, that does not end, while this one ends, and this is the meaning of "more lasting."

It has been said: what is meant by this provision is what God opens for the believers of spoils and the like. The first meaning is preferable, because the true superiority and the everlasting permanence that does not end can only be realized in the otherworldly provision, not the worldly one, even if it is lawful and good: ﴿What is with you will be exhausted, and what is with God is enduring﴾ [al-Nahl: 96].

﴿And enjoin your family to prayer﴾. God, glorified is He, commanded him to command his family to pray. What is meant by them is the people of his household. It has been said: all of his community. Here He did not mention the command from God to him to pray, but restricted the command to his family, either because his establishing it was a known matter, or because his command to it had already been given in His saying: ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise﴾ to the end of the verse, or because his command to them is a command to him. For this reason He said: ﴿and be steadfast in it﴾, that is, be patient in prayer, and do not occupy yourself from it with anything of the affairs of this world. ﴿We do not ask you for provision﴾, that is, We do not ask you to provide for yourself or your family and to occupy yourself with that away from prayer. ﴿We provide for you﴾, and We provide for them, and We do not burden you with that. ﴿And the final outcome is for righteousness﴾, that is, the praiseworthy final outcome, which is Paradise, belongs to the people of righteousness, with an omitted modifier (ellipsis of the mudaf), as al-Akhfash said. In this is evidence that righteousness is the essence of the matter, and upon it revolve the circles of goodness.

﴿And they say: Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾ That is, the disbelievers of Makkah said: Why does Muhammad not bring us a sign from the signs of his Lord, as the prophets before him brought them? Such as the she-camel and the staff. Or: Why does Muhammad not bring us one of the signs that we have proposed to him? God, glorified and exalted is He, answered them with His saying: ﴿Has there not come to them the clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾ By "the former scriptures" He means the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the rest of the revealed books, in which there is explicit mention of his prophethood and good tidings of him. That suffices, for these revealed books are acknowledged by them as true and sound, and in them is what repels their denial of his prophethood and nullifies their stubborn objections and forced arguments. It has been said: the meaning is: has there not come to them Our destruction of the nations that disbelieved and proposed signs? So what assures them that if the signs they proposed come to them, their situation will not be like theirs? It has been said: what is meant is: has there not come to them a sign that is the mother of signs and the greatest of them in the matter of miraculousness, meaning the Qur'an, for it is proof of what is in the rest of the revealed books. Abu Jaʿfar, Shaybah, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, Yaʿqub, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Hafs read ﴿Has there not come to them﴾ with the feminine taʾ. The rest read it with the masculine yaʾ, because the meaning of bayyinah (clear evidence) is explanation and proof, so they treated the verb according to the sense of bayyinah. Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim preferred this reading. Al-Kisa'i said: it is also permissible to read bayyinatun with tanwin. Al-Nahhas said: if it is given tanwin and read in the nominative, then ma is made a substitute for it, and if it is in the accusative, then it is in the circumstantial accusative. The meaning is: has there not come to them what is in the former scriptures clearly stated? This is according to what the grammatical permissibility requires, even if the recitation has not been transmitted with it.

﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾, that is, before the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ), or before the coming of the clear evidence, which is the revelation of the Qur'an, they would have said on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger﴾, that is, why did You not send to us a messenger in this world, ﴿so that we would have followed Your signs﴾ that the messenger brings, ﴿before we are humiliated﴾ by punishment in this world, ﴿and disgraced﴾ by entering the Fire. It has been read ﴿nudhall﴾ and ﴿nukhza﴾ in the passive voice. God has cut off the excuse of these disbelievers by sending the messenger to them before destroying them, and for this reason God relates of them that they ﴿said: Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied and said: God has not sent down anything﴾ [al-Mulk: 9].

﴿Say: Each is waiting, so wait﴾ (p-928) That is, say to them, O Muhammad: each one of us and of you is waiting, meaning awaiting what the matter will come to. So you wait, and ﴿you will soon know who are the companions of the even path﴾, that is, you will soon know, through victory and the outcome, who is among the companions of the straight path ﴿and who has been guided﴾ from error and turned away from deviation. The "who" in both places is in the nominative position as the subject of an inchoative (mubtada'). Al-Nahhas said: al-Farra' holds that the meaning of ﴿who are the companions of the even path﴾ is "who has not gone astray," and that the meaning of ﴿who has been guided﴾ is "who went astray and then was guided." It has also been said that "who" in both places is in the accusative position, and al-Farra' also said this. It is related from al-Zajjaj that he said: this is an error, because the interrogative does not take what precedes it as its governor. Abu Rafiʿ read ﴿so you will soon know﴾. Yahya ibn Yaʿmar and ʿAsim al-Jahdari read (al-siwwa) on the pattern fiʿla. This reading was rejected on the grounds that feminizing "path" is anomalous. It has also been said that it means the middle and the just.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾: "Did We not make clear to them ﴿how many generations We destroyed before them, who walk in their dwellings﴾", like ʿAd, Thamud, and whichever nations were destroyed. And regarding His saying ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been binding, and a specified term﴾: he said, "This is one of the advanced expressions of speech: he means, had it not been for a word and a specified term, it would have been binding." Ibn Abi Hatim related the same from al-Suddi. Ibn al-Mundhir related from Mujahid that he said: "The specified term is the word that preceded from your Lord." Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding ﴿it would have been binding﴾ that he said: "death." Al-Firyabi, ʿAbd al-Razzaq, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him regarding His saying ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise﴾, the verse, that he said: "It is the obligatory prayer." Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn ʿAsakir related from Jarir: "From the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun﴾, he said: 'Before the rising of the sun is the dawn prayer, and before its setting is the afternoon prayer.'"

In the two Sahih collections (al-Sahihayn, the two authentic compilations of Bukhari and Muslim) and others, from the hadith of Jarir, he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed you will see your Lord just as you see this moon; you will not be harmed in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so." Then he recited: ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾.

Also in Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abi Dawud and al-Nasa'i, on the authority of Imarah ibn Ruwaybah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No one who prays before the rising of the sun and before its setting will enter the Fire."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Rahawayh, al-Bazzar, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Kharaʾiti and Abu Nu'aym narrated on the authority of Abu Rafi', who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) hosted a guest, but the Prophet (ﷺ) did not have what would suffice him. So he sent me to a man of the Jews, saying: 'Sell us flour, or lend us flour, until the new moon of Rajab.' He said: 'No, except against a pledge.' So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him. He said: 'Truly, by Allah, I am trustworthy in the heaven and trustworthy on the earth. Had he lent it to me or sold it to me, I would have repaid him. Go with my new coat of mail (dir').' I had not left his presence before this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given to pairs of them, the splendor of the worldly life, that We may test them therein; but the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting﴾." It is as if [the verse] consoles him regarding the world.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, what I fear most for you is what Allah opens up for you of the splendor (zahrah) of the worldly life." They said: "What is the splendor of the worldly life, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The blessings of the earth."

Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Asakir and Ibn al-Najjar narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "When the verse was revealed: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) would come to the door of Ali at the time of the dawn prayer for eight months, saying: 'Prayer, may Allah have mercy upon you! ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House, and to purify you thoroughly﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33].'"

Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Abu al-Hamra'.

Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Thabit, who said: "When hardship befell his family, the Prophet (ﷺ) would call out to his family: 'O my family, pray, pray!'" Thabit said: "When a matter struck the Prophets, they would resort to prayer."

Abu 'Ubayd, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated through an isnad (chain of narrators) which al-Suyuti described as sahih (authentic), on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: "When hardship or constriction befell his family, the Prophet (ﷺ) would order them to pray, and he recited: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family﴾," the verse.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 20, verses 128–135 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾. The interrogative is for rebuke and reproach. The fa' (fa, "then") is for coordination with an implied antecedent, as has passed more than once. The clause is a fresh sentence (mustaʾnafah) to confirm what precedes it. The subject (fa'il) of yahdi ("become clear") is the clause mentioned after it, and its object (maf'ul) is omitted. The Basrans rejected this, because clauses do not function as subjects, while others permitted it.

Al-Qaffal said: "He made the large number of generations that We destroyed an explanation for them." Al-Nahhas said: "This is an error, because kam (how many) is an interrogative, so what precedes it does not govern it." Al-Zajjaj said: "The meaning is: Did not the matter of Our destroying those We destroyed make clear to them [the truth]? Its real sense indicates guidance, so the subject is guidance. And kam is in the accusative position governed by ahlakna (We destroyed)." It has also been said that the subject of yahdi is a pronoun referring to God or to the Messenger, and the clause after it explains it. The meaning of the verse, according to its apparent sense, is: Has it not become clear to the people of Makkah the report of those whom ﴿We destroyed before them of the generations﴾, while the generations ﴿walk in their dwellings﴾ and move about in their homes? Or [the meaning is] while these [Makkans] walk in the dwellings of the generations whom We destroyed, when they go out for trade and to seek livelihood, so they see the lands of the past nations and the bygone generations, desolate and ruined, [including] the Companions of the Rass, Thamud, and the towns of the people of Lut. Indeed, that is among the things that necessitate reflection on them, lest there befall them what befell those [earlier peoples]. Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Sulami read (nahdi) with the nun, and the meaning on this reading is clear. The clause ﴿Indeed in that are signs for people of intellect﴾ is a justification for the rebuke and a confirmation of the guidance. The demonstrative "that" refers to the content of "how many We destroyed," and so on to the end.

Al-Nuha is the plural of nuhyah, which means intellect, that is, for those possessing minds that restrain their owners from what is ugly.

﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, that is, had it not been for the preceding word, which is God's promise to delay the punishment of this community until the Hereafter, the punishment for their sins would have been lazim (inevitable), meaning necessarily binding upon them, not separating from them in any state and not delayed. His saying: ﴿and a specified term﴾ is coordinated with "word," as al-Zajjaj and others said. The specified term is the Day of Resurrection, or the Day of Badr. Al-Lizam is the verbal noun of lazima. It has been said that it is permissible to coordinate "a specified term" with the hidden pronoun in "would have been," which refers to the immediate punishment understood from the context, treating the separation by the predicate as equivalent to emphasis. That is: the immediate seizing and "a specified term" would have been binding upon them, as they were binding upon ʿAd and Thamud. But this is clearly strained.

Then, when God, glorified is He, made clear that He would not destroy them with the punishment of total annihilation, He commanded him to be patient, saying: ﴿So be patient over what they say﴾, meaning that you are a sorcerer and a liar, and similar of their false slanders. The meaning is: do not concern yourself with them, for their punishment has an appointed time that will neither come early nor late. It has been said that this is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of fighting. ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise﴾, that is, while being clothed in His praise. Most of the exegetes said: what is meant is the five prayers, as His saying indicates: ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾, which refers to the dawn prayer, ﴿and before its setting﴾, which refers to the afternoon prayer, ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾, meaning the ʿatamah (night prayer). Al-anaʾ (hours) means the periods, and it is the plural of inan with a kasra and short vowel, meaning an hour. The meaning of "glorify" is "pray." ﴿And the extremities of the day﴾, that is, the sunset (maghrib) and noon (zuhr) prayers, because noon falls at the end of the first extremity of the day and the beginning of the other extremity. It has been said that the reference to the noon prayer is in His saying ﴿and before its setting﴾, because the noon prayer and the afternoon prayer both occur before the sun sets. It has also been said that what is meant by the verse is voluntary prayer (tatawwuʿ). It could be said that there is no reference to prayer in the verse, but rather what is meant is glorification (tasbih) during these times, that is, the saying of one who says "Glory be to God." That would not be far from correct. Glorification during these times, although it may be applied to prayer, is metaphorical (majaz), and the literal meaning (haqiqah) takes priority unless there is an indicator that turns it toward the figurative sense. His saying: ﴿so that you may be pleased﴾ is connected to "so glorify": that is, glorify during these times in hope that you will attain from God, glorified is He, what your soul is pleased with. This is according to the reading of the majority. Al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim read (turda, "you are pleased") with a damma on the taʾ in the passive voice, meaning: your Lord will be pleased with you.

﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to of them, as pairs﴾. The exegesis of this verse has already been given in al-Hijr. The meaning is: do not prolong the gaze of your eyes. "Azwajan" is the object (maf'ul) of "We have given enjoyment." "Zahrata" is in the accusative, either as a circumstantial accusative (hal) or governed by an implied verb, meaning "We made" or "We gave." Al-Zajjaj mentioned this meaning. It has also been said that it is a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in "with it," with regard to its position, which is the accusative, not with regard to its form, since it is in the genitive, as you say "I passed by him, your brother." Al-Farra' preferred the accusative as a circumstantial accusative, and it is permissible that it be a substitute, and it is permissible that it be in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar), like ﴿the dye of God﴾ and ﴿the promise of God﴾ and ﴿the splendor of the worldly life﴾. Its meaning is its adornment and brilliance with plants and other things. ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar read (zahrata) with a fatha on the ha', which is the blossom of plants. The lam in "that We may test them therein" is connected to "We have given enjoyment": that is, that We make that a trial for them and a misguidance, as a test from Us for them, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them﴾ [al-Kahf: 7]. It has also been said: that We may punish them. And it has been said: that We may make the obligations heavier upon them. ﴿And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting﴾, that is, the reward of God, and what He has stored up for His righteous servants in the Hereafter is better than what He provided them in this world in every state. Moreover, that does not end, while this one ends, and this is the meaning of "more lasting."

It has been said: what is meant by this provision is what God opens for the believers of spoils and the like. The first meaning is preferable, because the true superiority and the everlasting permanence that does not end can only be realized in the otherworldly provision, not the worldly one, even if it is lawful and good: ﴿What is with you will be exhausted, and what is with God is enduring﴾ [al-Nahl: 96].

﴿And enjoin your family to prayer﴾. God, glorified is He, commanded him to command his family to pray. What is meant by them is the people of his household. It has been said: all of his community. Here He did not mention the command from God to him to pray, but restricted the command to his family, either because his establishing it was a known matter, or because his command to it had already been given in His saying: ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise﴾ to the end of the verse, or because his command to them is a command to him. For this reason He said: ﴿and be steadfast in it﴾, that is, be patient in prayer, and do not occupy yourself from it with anything of the affairs of this world. ﴿We do not ask you for provision﴾, that is, We do not ask you to provide for yourself or your family and to occupy yourself with that away from prayer. ﴿We provide for you﴾, and We provide for them, and We do not burden you with that. ﴿And the final outcome is for righteousness﴾, that is, the praiseworthy final outcome, which is Paradise, belongs to the people of righteousness, with an omitted modifier (ellipsis of the mudaf), as al-Akhfash said. In this is evidence that righteousness is the essence of the matter, and upon it revolve the circles of goodness.

﴿And they say: Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾ That is, the disbelievers of Makkah said: Why does Muhammad not bring us a sign from the signs of his Lord, as the prophets before him brought them? Such as the she-camel and the staff. Or: Why does Muhammad not bring us one of the signs that we have proposed to him? God, glorified and exalted is He, answered them with His saying: ﴿Has there not come to them the clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾ By "the former scriptures" He means the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the rest of the revealed books, in which there is explicit mention of his prophethood and good tidings of him. That suffices, for these revealed books are acknowledged by them as true and sound, and in them is what repels their denial of his prophethood and nullifies their stubborn objections and forced arguments. It has been said: the meaning is: has there not come to them Our destruction of the nations that disbelieved and proposed signs? So what assures them that if the signs they proposed come to them, their situation will not be like theirs? It has been said: what is meant is: has there not come to them a sign that is the mother of signs and the greatest of them in the matter of miraculousness, meaning the Qur'an, for it is proof of what is in the rest of the revealed books. Abu Jaʿfar, Shaybah, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, Yaʿqub, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Hafs read ﴿Has there not come to them﴾ with the feminine taʾ. The rest read it with the masculine yaʾ, because the meaning of bayyinah (clear evidence) is explanation and proof, so they treated the verb according to the sense of bayyinah. Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim preferred this reading. Al-Kisa'i said: it is also permissible to read bayyinatun with tanwin. Al-Nahhas said: if it is given tanwin and read in the nominative, then ma is made a substitute for it, and if it is in the accusative, then it is in the circumstantial accusative. The meaning is: has there not come to them what is in the former scriptures clearly stated? This is according to what the grammatical permissibility requires, even if the recitation has not been transmitted with it.

﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾, that is, before the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ), or before the coming of the clear evidence, which is the revelation of the Qur'an, they would have said on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger﴾, that is, why did You not send to us a messenger in this world, ﴿so that we would have followed Your signs﴾ that the messenger brings, ﴿before we are humiliated﴾ by punishment in this world, ﴿and disgraced﴾ by entering the Fire. It has been read ﴿nudhall﴾ and ﴿nukhza﴾ in the passive voice. God has cut off the excuse of these disbelievers by sending the messenger to them before destroying them, and for this reason God relates of them that they ﴿said: Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied and said: God has not sent down anything﴾ [al-Mulk: 9].

﴿Say: Each is waiting, so wait﴾ (p-928) That is, say to them, O Muhammad: each one of us and of you is waiting, meaning awaiting what the matter will come to. So you wait, and ﴿you will soon know who are the companions of the even path﴾, that is, you will soon know, through victory and the outcome, who is among the companions of the straight path ﴿and who has been guided﴾ from error and turned away from deviation. The "who" in both places is in the nominative position as the subject of an inchoative (mubtada'). Al-Nahhas said: al-Farra' holds that the meaning of ﴿who are the companions of the even path﴾ is "who has not gone astray," and that the meaning of ﴿who has been guided﴾ is "who went astray and then was guided." It has also been said that "who" in both places is in the accusative position, and al-Farra' also said this. It is related from al-Zajjaj that he said: this is an error, because the interrogative does not take what precedes it as its governor. Abu Rafiʿ read ﴿so you will soon know﴾. Yahya ibn Yaʿmar and ʿAsim al-Jahdari read (al-siwwa) on the pattern fiʿla. This reading was rejected on the grounds that feminizing "path" is anomalous. It has also been said that it means the middle and the just.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾: "Did We not make clear to them ﴿how many generations We destroyed before them, who walk in their dwellings﴾", like ʿAd, Thamud, and whichever nations were destroyed. And regarding His saying ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been binding, and a specified term﴾: he said, "This is one of the advanced expressions of speech: he means, had it not been for a word and a specified term, it would have been binding." Ibn Abi Hatim related the same from al-Suddi. Ibn al-Mundhir related from Mujahid that he said: "The specified term is the word that preceded from your Lord." Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding ﴿it would have been binding﴾ that he said: "death." Al-Firyabi, ʿAbd al-Razzaq, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him regarding His saying ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise﴾, the verse, that he said: "It is the obligatory prayer." Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn ʿAsakir related from Jarir: "From the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun﴾, he said: 'Before the rising of the sun is the dawn prayer, and before its setting is the afternoon prayer.'"

In the two Sahih collections (al-Sahihayn, the two authentic compilations of Bukhari and Muslim) and others, from the hadith of Jarir, he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed you will see your Lord just as you see this moon; you will not be harmed in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so." Then he recited: ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾.

Also in Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abi Dawud and al-Nasa'i, on the authority of Imarah ibn Ruwaybah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No one who prays before the rising of the sun and before its setting will enter the Fire."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Rahawayh, al-Bazzar, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Kharaʾiti and Abu Nu'aym narrated on the authority of Abu Rafi', who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) hosted a guest, but the Prophet (ﷺ) did not have what would suffice him. So he sent me to a man of the Jews, saying: 'Sell us flour, or lend us flour, until the new moon of Rajab.' He said: 'No, except against a pledge.' So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him. He said: 'Truly, by Allah, I am trustworthy in the heaven and trustworthy on the earth. Had he lent it to me or sold it to me, I would have repaid him. Go with my new coat of mail (dir').' I had not left his presence before this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given to pairs of them, the splendor of the worldly life, that We may test them therein; but the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting﴾." It is as if [the verse] consoles him regarding the world.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, what I fear most for you is what Allah opens up for you of the splendor (zahrah) of the worldly life." They said: "What is the splendor of the worldly life, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The blessings of the earth."

Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Asakir and Ibn al-Najjar narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "When the verse was revealed: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) would come to the door of Ali at the time of the dawn prayer for eight months, saying: 'Prayer, may Allah have mercy upon you! ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House, and to purify you thoroughly﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33].'"

Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Abu al-Hamra'.

Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Thabit, who said: "When hardship befell his family, the Prophet (ﷺ) would call out to his family: 'O my family, pray, pray!'" Thabit said: "When a matter struck the Prophets, they would resort to prayer."

Abu 'Ubayd, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated through an isnad (chain of narrators) which al-Suyuti described as sahih (authentic), on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: "When hardship or constriction befell his family, the Prophet (ﷺ) would order them to pray, and he recited: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family﴾," the verse.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 20, verses 128–135 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾. The interrogative is for rebuke and reproach. The fa' (fa, "then") is for coordination with an implied antecedent, as has passed more than once. The clause is a fresh sentence (mustaʾnafah) to confirm what precedes it. The subject (fa'il) of yahdi ("become clear") is the clause mentioned after it, and its object (maf'ul) is omitted. The Basrans rejected this, because clauses do not function as subjects, while others permitted it.

Al-Qaffal said: "He made the large number of generations that We destroyed an explanation for them." Al-Nahhas said: "This is an error, because kam (how many) is an interrogative, so what precedes it does not govern it." Al-Zajjaj said: "The meaning is: Did not the matter of Our destroying those We destroyed make clear to them [the truth]? Its real sense indicates guidance, so the subject is guidance. And kam is in the accusative position governed by ahlakna (We destroyed)." It has also been said that the subject of yahdi is a pronoun referring to God or to the Messenger, and the clause after it explains it. The meaning of the verse, according to its apparent sense, is: Has it not become clear to the people of Makkah the report of those whom ﴿We destroyed before them of the generations﴾, while the generations ﴿walk in their dwellings﴾ and move about in their homes? Or [the meaning is] while these [Makkans] walk in the dwellings of the generations whom We destroyed, when they go out for trade and to seek livelihood, so they see the lands of the past nations and the bygone generations, desolate and ruined, [including] the Companions of the Rass, Thamud, and the towns of the people of Lut. Indeed, that is among the things that necessitate reflection on them, lest there befall them what befell those [earlier peoples]. Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Sulami read (nahdi) with the nun, and the meaning on this reading is clear. The clause ﴿Indeed in that are signs for people of intellect﴾ is a justification for the rebuke and a confirmation of the guidance. The demonstrative "that" refers to the content of "how many We destroyed," and so on to the end.

Al-Nuha is the plural of nuhyah, which means intellect, that is, for those possessing minds that restrain their owners from what is ugly.

﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, that is, had it not been for the preceding word, which is God's promise to delay the punishment of this community until the Hereafter, the punishment for their sins would have been lazim (inevitable), meaning necessarily binding upon them, not separating from them in any state and not delayed. His saying: ﴿and a specified term﴾ is coordinated with "word," as al-Zajjaj and others said. The specified term is the Day of Resurrection, or the Day of Badr. Al-Lizam is the verbal noun of lazima. It has been said that it is permissible to coordinate "a specified term" with the hidden pronoun in "would have been," which refers to the immediate punishment understood from the context, treating the separation by the predicate as equivalent to emphasis. That is: the immediate seizing and "a specified term" would have been binding upon them, as they were binding upon ʿAd and Thamud. But this is clearly strained.

Then, when God, glorified is He, made clear that He would not destroy them with the punishment of total annihilation, He commanded him to be patient, saying: ﴿So be patient over what they say﴾, meaning that you are a sorcerer and a liar, and similar of their false slanders. The meaning is: do not concern yourself with them, for their punishment has an appointed time that will neither come early nor late. It has been said that this is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of fighting. ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise﴾, that is, while being clothed in His praise. Most of the exegetes said: what is meant is the five prayers, as His saying indicates: ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾, which refers to the dawn prayer, ﴿and before its setting﴾, which refers to the afternoon prayer, ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾, meaning the ʿatamah (night prayer). Al-anaʾ (hours) means the periods, and it is the plural of inan with a kasra and short vowel, meaning an hour. The meaning of "glorify" is "pray." ﴿And the extremities of the day﴾, that is, the sunset (maghrib) and noon (zuhr) prayers, because noon falls at the end of the first extremity of the day and the beginning of the other extremity. It has been said that the reference to the noon prayer is in His saying ﴿and before its setting﴾, because the noon prayer and the afternoon prayer both occur before the sun sets. It has also been said that what is meant by the verse is voluntary prayer (tatawwuʿ). It could be said that there is no reference to prayer in the verse, but rather what is meant is glorification (tasbih) during these times, that is, the saying of one who says "Glory be to God." That would not be far from correct. Glorification during these times, although it may be applied to prayer, is metaphorical (majaz), and the literal meaning (haqiqah) takes priority unless there is an indicator that turns it toward the figurative sense. His saying: ﴿so that you may be pleased﴾ is connected to "so glorify": that is, glorify during these times in hope that you will attain from God, glorified is He, what your soul is pleased with. This is according to the reading of the majority. Al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim read (turda, "you are pleased") with a damma on the taʾ in the passive voice, meaning: your Lord will be pleased with you.

﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to of them, as pairs﴾. The exegesis of this verse has already been given in al-Hijr. The meaning is: do not prolong the gaze of your eyes. "Azwajan" is the object (maf'ul) of "We have given enjoyment." "Zahrata" is in the accusative, either as a circumstantial accusative (hal) or governed by an implied verb, meaning "We made" or "We gave." Al-Zajjaj mentioned this meaning. It has also been said that it is a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in "with it," with regard to its position, which is the accusative, not with regard to its form, since it is in the genitive, as you say "I passed by him, your brother." Al-Farra' preferred the accusative as a circumstantial accusative, and it is permissible that it be a substitute, and it is permissible that it be in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar), like ﴿the dye of God﴾ and ﴿the promise of God﴾ and ﴿the splendor of the worldly life﴾. Its meaning is its adornment and brilliance with plants and other things. ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar read (zahrata) with a fatha on the ha', which is the blossom of plants. The lam in "that We may test them therein" is connected to "We have given enjoyment": that is, that We make that a trial for them and a misguidance, as a test from Us for them, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them﴾ [al-Kahf: 7]. It has also been said: that We may punish them. And it has been said: that We may make the obligations heavier upon them. ﴿And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting﴾, that is, the reward of God, and what He has stored up for His righteous servants in the Hereafter is better than what He provided them in this world in every state. Moreover, that does not end, while this one ends, and this is the meaning of "more lasting."

It has been said: what is meant by this provision is what God opens for the believers of spoils and the like. The first meaning is preferable, because the true superiority and the everlasting permanence that does not end can only be realized in the otherworldly provision, not the worldly one, even if it is lawful and good: ﴿What is with you will be exhausted, and what is with God is enduring﴾ [al-Nahl: 96].

﴿And enjoin your family to prayer﴾. God, glorified is He, commanded him to command his family to pray. What is meant by them is the people of his household. It has been said: all of his community. Here He did not mention the command from God to him to pray, but restricted the command to his family, either because his establishing it was a known matter, or because his command to it had already been given in His saying: ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise﴾ to the end of the verse, or because his command to them is a command to him. For this reason He said: ﴿and be steadfast in it﴾, that is, be patient in prayer, and do not occupy yourself from it with anything of the affairs of this world. ﴿We do not ask you for provision﴾, that is, We do not ask you to provide for yourself or your family and to occupy yourself with that away from prayer. ﴿We provide for you﴾, and We provide for them, and We do not burden you with that. ﴿And the final outcome is for righteousness﴾, that is, the praiseworthy final outcome, which is Paradise, belongs to the people of righteousness, with an omitted modifier (ellipsis of the mudaf), as al-Akhfash said. In this is evidence that righteousness is the essence of the matter, and upon it revolve the circles of goodness.

﴿And they say: Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾ That is, the disbelievers of Makkah said: Why does Muhammad not bring us a sign from the signs of his Lord, as the prophets before him brought them? Such as the she-camel and the staff. Or: Why does Muhammad not bring us one of the signs that we have proposed to him? God, glorified and exalted is He, answered them with His saying: ﴿Has there not come to them the clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾ By "the former scriptures" He means the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the rest of the revealed books, in which there is explicit mention of his prophethood and good tidings of him. That suffices, for these revealed books are acknowledged by them as true and sound, and in them is what repels their denial of his prophethood and nullifies their stubborn objections and forced arguments. It has been said: the meaning is: has there not come to them Our destruction of the nations that disbelieved and proposed signs? So what assures them that if the signs they proposed come to them, their situation will not be like theirs? It has been said: what is meant is: has there not come to them a sign that is the mother of signs and the greatest of them in the matter of miraculousness, meaning the Qur'an, for it is proof of what is in the rest of the revealed books. Abu Jaʿfar, Shaybah, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, Yaʿqub, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Hafs read ﴿Has there not come to them﴾ with the feminine taʾ. The rest read it with the masculine yaʾ, because the meaning of bayyinah (clear evidence) is explanation and proof, so they treated the verb according to the sense of bayyinah. Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim preferred this reading. Al-Kisa'i said: it is also permissible to read bayyinatun with tanwin. Al-Nahhas said: if it is given tanwin and read in the nominative, then ma is made a substitute for it, and if it is in the accusative, then it is in the circumstantial accusative. The meaning is: has there not come to them what is in the former scriptures clearly stated? This is according to what the grammatical permissibility requires, even if the recitation has not been transmitted with it.

﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾, that is, before the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ), or before the coming of the clear evidence, which is the revelation of the Qur'an, they would have said on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger﴾, that is, why did You not send to us a messenger in this world, ﴿so that we would have followed Your signs﴾ that the messenger brings, ﴿before we are humiliated﴾ by punishment in this world, ﴿and disgraced﴾ by entering the Fire. It has been read ﴿nudhall﴾ and ﴿nukhza﴾ in the passive voice. God has cut off the excuse of these disbelievers by sending the messenger to them before destroying them, and for this reason God relates of them that they ﴿said: Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied and said: God has not sent down anything﴾ [al-Mulk: 9].

﴿Say: Each is waiting, so wait﴾ (p-928) That is, say to them, O Muhammad: each one of us and of you is waiting, meaning awaiting what the matter will come to. So you wait, and ﴿you will soon know who are the companions of the even path﴾, that is, you will soon know, through victory and the outcome, who is among the companions of the straight path ﴿and who has been guided﴾ from error and turned away from deviation. The "who" in both places is in the nominative position as the subject of an inchoative (mubtada'). Al-Nahhas said: al-Farra' holds that the meaning of ﴿who are the companions of the even path﴾ is "who has not gone astray," and that the meaning of ﴿who has been guided﴾ is "who went astray and then was guided." It has also been said that "who" in both places is in the accusative position, and al-Farra' also said this. It is related from al-Zajjaj that he said: this is an error, because the interrogative does not take what precedes it as its governor. Abu Rafiʿ read ﴿so you will soon know﴾. Yahya ibn Yaʿmar and ʿAsim al-Jahdari read (al-siwwa) on the pattern fiʿla. This reading was rejected on the grounds that feminizing "path" is anomalous. It has also been said that it means the middle and the just.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾: "Did We not make clear to them ﴿how many generations We destroyed before them, who walk in their dwellings﴾", like ʿAd, Thamud, and whichever nations were destroyed. And regarding His saying ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been binding, and a specified term﴾: he said, "This is one of the advanced expressions of speech: he means, had it not been for a word and a specified term, it would have been binding." Ibn Abi Hatim related the same from al-Suddi. Ibn al-Mundhir related from Mujahid that he said: "The specified term is the word that preceded from your Lord." Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding ﴿it would have been binding﴾ that he said: "death." Al-Firyabi, ʿAbd al-Razzaq, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him regarding His saying ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise﴾, the verse, that he said: "It is the obligatory prayer." Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn ʿAsakir related from Jarir: "From the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun﴾, he said: 'Before the rising of the sun is the dawn prayer, and before its setting is the afternoon prayer.'"

In the two Sahih collections (al-Sahihayn, the two authentic compilations of Bukhari and Muslim) and others, from the hadith of Jarir, he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed you will see your Lord just as you see this moon; you will not be harmed in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so." Then he recited: ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾.

Also in Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abi Dawud and al-Nasa'i, on the authority of Imarah ibn Ruwaybah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No one who prays before the rising of the sun and before its setting will enter the Fire."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Rahawayh, al-Bazzar, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Kharaʾiti and Abu Nu'aym narrated on the authority of Abu Rafi', who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) hosted a guest, but the Prophet (ﷺ) did not have what would suffice him. So he sent me to a man of the Jews, saying: 'Sell us flour, or lend us flour, until the new moon of Rajab.' He said: 'No, except against a pledge.' So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him. He said: 'Truly, by Allah, I am trustworthy in the heaven and trustworthy on the earth. Had he lent it to me or sold it to me, I would have repaid him. Go with my new coat of mail (dir').' I had not left his presence before this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given to pairs of them, the splendor of the worldly life, that We may test them therein; but the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting﴾." It is as if [the verse] consoles him regarding the world.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, what I fear most for you is what Allah opens up for you of the splendor (zahrah) of the worldly life." They said: "What is the splendor of the worldly life, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The blessings of the earth."

Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Asakir and Ibn al-Najjar narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "When the verse was revealed: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) would come to the door of Ali at the time of the dawn prayer for eight months, saying: 'Prayer, may Allah have mercy upon you! ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House, and to purify you thoroughly﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33].'"

Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Abu al-Hamra'.

Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Thabit, who said: "When hardship befell his family, the Prophet (ﷺ) would call out to his family: 'O my family, pray, pray!'" Thabit said: "When a matter struck the Prophets, they would resort to prayer."

Abu 'Ubayd, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated through an isnad (chain of narrators) which al-Suyuti described as sahih (authentic), on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: "When hardship or constriction befell his family, the Prophet (ﷺ) would order them to pray, and he recited: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family﴾," the verse.

It has been said: what is meant by this provision is what God opens for the believers of spoils and the like. The first meaning is preferable, because the true superiority and the everlasting permanence that does not end can only be realized in the otherworldly provision, not the worldly one, even if it is lawful and good: ﴿What is with you will be exhausted, and what is with God is enduring﴾ [al-Nahl: 96].

﴿And enjoin your family to prayer﴾. God, glorified is He, commanded him to command his family to pray. What is meant by them is the people of his household. It has been said: all of his community. Here He did not mention the command from God to him to pray, but restricted the command to his family, either because his establishing it was a known matter, or because his command to it had already been given in His saying: ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise﴾ to the end of the verse, or because his command to them is a command to him. For this reason He said: ﴿and be steadfast in it﴾, that is, be patient in prayer, and do not occupy yourself from it with anything of the affairs of this world. ﴿We do not ask you for provision﴾, that is, We do not ask you to provide for yourself or your family and to occupy yourself with that away from prayer. ﴿We provide for you﴾, and We provide for them, and We do not burden you with that. ﴿And the final outcome is for righteousness﴾, that is, the praiseworthy final outcome, which is Paradise, belongs to the people of righteousness, with an omitted modifier (ellipsis of the mudaf), as al-Akhfash said. In this is evidence that righteousness is the essence of the matter, and upon it revolve the circles of goodness.

﴿And they say: Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾ That is, the disbelievers of Makkah said: Why does Muhammad not bring us a sign from the signs of his Lord, as the prophets before him brought them? Such as the she-camel and the staff. Or: Why does Muhammad not bring us one of the signs that we have proposed to him? God, glorified and exalted is He, answered them with His saying: ﴿Has there not come to them the clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾ By "the former scriptures" He means the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the rest of the revealed books, in which there is explicit mention of his prophethood and good tidings of him. That suffices, for these revealed books are acknowledged by them as true and sound, and in them is what repels their denial of his prophethood and nullifies their stubborn objections and forced arguments. It has been said: the meaning is: has there not come to them Our destruction of the nations that disbelieved and proposed signs? So what assures them that if the signs they proposed come to them, their situation will not be like theirs? It has been said: what is meant is: has there not come to them a sign that is the mother of signs and the greatest of them in the matter of miraculousness, meaning the Qur'an, for it is proof of what is in the rest of the revealed books. Abu Jaʿfar, Shaybah, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, Yaʿqub, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Hafs read ﴿Has there not come to them﴾ with the feminine taʾ. The rest read it with the masculine yaʾ, because the meaning of bayyinah (clear evidence) is explanation and proof, so they treated the verb according to the sense of bayyinah. Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim preferred this reading. Al-Kisa'i said: it is also permissible to read bayyinatun with tanwin. Al-Nahhas said: if it is given tanwin and read in the nominative, then ma is made a substitute for it, and if it is in the accusative, then it is in the circumstantial accusative. The meaning is: has there not come to them what is in the former scriptures clearly stated? This is according to what the grammatical permissibility requires, even if the recitation has not been transmitted with it.

﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾, that is, before the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ), or before the coming of the clear evidence, which is the revelation of the Qur'an, they would have said on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger﴾, that is, why did You not send to us a messenger in this world, ﴿so that we would have followed Your signs﴾ that the messenger brings, ﴿before we are humiliated﴾ by punishment in this world, ﴿and disgraced﴾ by entering the Fire. It has been read ﴿nudhall﴾ and ﴿nukhza﴾ in the passive voice. God has cut off the excuse of these disbelievers by sending the messenger to them before destroying them, and for this reason God relates of them that they ﴿said: Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied and said: God has not sent down anything﴾ [al-Mulk: 9].

﴿Say: Each is waiting, so wait﴾ (p-928) That is, say to them, O Muhammad: each one of us and of you is waiting, meaning awaiting what the matter will come to. So you wait, and ﴿you will soon know who are the companions of the even path﴾, that is, you will soon know, through victory and the outcome, who is among the companions of the straight path ﴿and who has been guided﴾ from error and turned away from deviation. The "who" in both places is in the nominative position as the subject of an inchoative (mubtada'). Al-Nahhas said: al-Farra' holds that the meaning of ﴿who are the companions of the even path﴾ is "who has not gone astray," and that the meaning of ﴿who has been guided﴾ is "who went astray and then was guided." It has also been said that "who" in both places is in the accusative position, and al-Farra' also said this. It is related from al-Zajjaj that he said: this is an error, because the interrogative does not take what precedes it as its governor. Abu Rafiʿ read ﴿so you will soon know﴾. Yahya ibn Yaʿmar and ʿAsim al-Jahdari read (al-siwwa) on the pattern fiʿla. This reading was rejected on the grounds that feminizing "path" is anomalous. It has also been said that it means the middle and the just.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾: "Did We not make clear to them ﴿how many generations We destroyed before them, who walk in their dwellings﴾", like ʿAd, Thamud, and whichever nations were destroyed. And regarding His saying ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been binding, and a specified term﴾: he said, "This is one of the advanced expressions of speech: he means, had it not been for a word and a specified term, it would have been binding." Ibn Abi Hatim related the same from al-Suddi. Ibn al-Mundhir related from Mujahid that he said: "The specified term is the word that preceded from your Lord." Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding ﴿it would have been binding﴾ that he said: "death." Al-Firyabi, ʿAbd al-Razzaq, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him regarding His saying ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise﴾, the verse, that he said: "It is the obligatory prayer." Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn ʿAsakir related from Jarir: "From the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun﴾, he said: 'Before the rising of the sun is the dawn prayer, and before its setting is the afternoon prayer.'"

In the two Sahih collections (al-Sahihayn, the two authentic compilations of Bukhari and Muslim) and others, from the hadith of Jarir, he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed you will see your Lord just as you see this moon; you will not be harmed in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so." Then he recited: ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾.

Also in Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abi Dawud and al-Nasa'i, on the authority of Imarah ibn Ruwaybah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No one who prays before the rising of the sun and before its setting will enter the Fire."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Rahawayh, al-Bazzar, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Kharaʾiti and Abu Nu'aym narrated on the authority of Abu Rafi', who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) hosted a guest, but the Prophet (ﷺ) did not have what would suffice him. So he sent me to a man of the Jews, saying: 'Sell us flour, or lend us flour, until the new moon of Rajab.' He said: 'No, except against a pledge.' So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him. He said: 'Truly, by Allah, I am trustworthy in the heaven and trustworthy on the earth. Had he lent it to me or sold it to me, I would have repaid him. Go with my new coat of mail (dir').' I had not left his presence before this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given to pairs of them, the splendor of the worldly life, that We may test them therein; but the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting﴾." It is as if [the verse] consoles him regarding the world.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, what I fear most for you is what Allah opens up for you of the splendor (zahrah) of the worldly life." They said: "What is the splendor of the worldly life, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The blessings of the earth."

Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Asakir and Ibn al-Najjar narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "When the verse was revealed: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) would come to the door of Ali at the time of the dawn prayer for eight months, saying: 'Prayer, may Allah have mercy upon you! ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House, and to purify you thoroughly﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33].'"

Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Abu al-Hamra'.

Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Thabit, who said: "When hardship befell his family, the Prophet (ﷺ) would call out to his family: 'O my family, pray, pray!'" Thabit said: "When a matter struck the Prophets, they would resort to prayer."

Abu 'Ubayd, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated through an isnad (chain of narrators) which al-Suyuti described as sahih (authentic), on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: "When hardship or constriction befell his family, the Prophet (ﷺ) would order them to pray, and he recited: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family﴾," the verse.
